title: "All reasonable steps": harassment-prevention evidence for UK SMEs

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: A dated legal duty with tribunal exposure and an explicit evidence requirement; frequency is low (periodic legal event) but severity is material.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: Buyer identified (SME owner/office manager) but budget is inferred; free official content creates price pressure; capped at 2.

evidence_strength.rationale: Primary legislation plus official Acas/gov.uk material establish the duty and date; buyer-side demand evidence is absent.

distribution.rationale: Fragmented SME buyer; accountant/lawyer referrals and direct outreach are plausible only (capped at 2).

differentiation.rationale: No dedicated low-cost SME tool surfaced, but free authoritative guidance and generalist HR platforms are close substitutes.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: A 10-interview price/commitment test is cheap and fast; decision rule fixed in advance.

feasibility.rationale: Templates plus a simple record-keeping tool are low-complexity and low-support.

economics.rationale: Modelled only and untested (capped at 2); free official content limits pricing power.

founder_fit.rationale: Inferred fit for a founder with HR/compliance content and SME distribution; no owner-specific evidence.

risk.rationale: Handling harassment records is sensitive; the tool must avoid giving legal advice. Review policy trigger 4 (legal/regulatory/trust risk) should be assessed by the human owner before external testing.

economic_buyer.note: SME owner/office manager is identifiable, but budget for this specific job is inferred, not evidenced.
economic_buyer.resolve_via: Proposed experiment tests a concrete >=£12/mo commitment from 10 target employers.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: The legal duty is evidenced; whether owners feel enough pain to act before 30 Oct 2026 is not.
painful_frequent_or_budgeted.resolve_via: Interview urgency and current practice in the proposed experiment.

non_paid_distribution.note: Accountant/lawyer referrals and direct outreach are plausible, not evidenced.
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: Test one non-network recruitment channel for >=5 conversations.

defensible_wedge.note: No dedicated low-cost SME evidence tool surfaced, but free Acas/EHRC content and generalist HR platforms are close substitutes; the wedge is the specific evidence/audit job, not content.
defensible_wedge.resolve_via: Broader competitor search and prototype interviews to confirm no dedicated tool and that the evidence job (not the content) is what buyers value.

no_network_effects_needed.note: Likely per-customer value with no density requirement; not explicitly tested.
no_network_effects_needed.resolve_via: Confirm a single employer can use it standalone.

plausible_margins.note: No cost or conversion evidence; free official content constrains price.
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Model support/content cost against a tested >=£12/mo price.

acceptable_risk.note: Sensitive personal data and potential perceived legal advice; must be scoped carefully.
acceptable_risk.resolve_via: Privacy/legal scoping before any build; human owner to assess review trigger 4.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: The proposed 10-interview commitment test is cheap (£20, 10 hours, 7 days) and has a pre-fixed decision rule and kill condition capable of disconfirming the central assumption.

not_all_optimistic.note: Viability does not require every assumption, but it does require owners to pay for something adjacent to free guidance; not yet shown.
not_all_optimistic.resolve_via: Proposed experiment is designed to test the central assumption first.
